Title: Madrid acolhe final da Liga dos Campeões pela nona vez

Summary: 
On September 11, 2025, the UEFA Executive Committee confirmed that the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid will host the 2026/27 Champions League final, marking the ninth time Spain will host the competition and the fourth in the Champions League format. The 70,000‑seat stadium, opened in 2017, had previously hosted the 2018/19 final where Liverpool beat Tottenham 2‑0. The decision followed the withdrawal of Milan’s San Siro bid in October 2024 due to planned renovations. Spain has hosted the final eight times before: four at Santiago Bernabéu (1956/57, 1968/69, 1979/80, 2009/10), one at Metropolitano (2018/19), two at Camp Nou (1988/89, 1998/99) and one at Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán (1985/86). The Metropolitano is also on the list of venues for the 2030 World Cup bid by Portugal, Spain and Morocco. UEFA also appointed Red Bull Arena in Salzburg for the 2026 European Super Cup and the National Stadium in Warsaw for the 2026/27 Women’s Champions League final. In futsal, the 2025 Champions League final will be in Pesaro, Italy, while the 2027 U19 men’s and women’s European finals will be in Astana, Kazakhstan and Osijek, Croatia respectively. UEFA approved a rule change for the 2025/26 club season allowing a temporary replacement of up to one outfield player with a long‑term injury or illness until the sixth matchday of each league phase. ‘The reason for the adaptation is to ensure that the squads are not unfairly reduced and that players are protected from the additional workload pressure,’ said the organization led by Slovenian Aleksander Ceferin. The Executive Committee also discussed requests from the RFEF and FIGC to hold national championship matches outside their home countries, but will seek input from all stakeholders before deciding. The next meeting is scheduled for December 3 in Nyon, Switzerland.
